The IPO is typically when a company rakes in operating money, although the company can "print" stock at any time - but doing so devalues the stock already in circulation.
Any loss of "worth" in the stocks just allows anyone that wants to take over a better opportunity.

Example1: Amazon. Suppose Bozo holds 60% of the Amazon stock. Even if the stock dropped to $1, if Bozo didn't want to sell, he would still be able to control the company. He couldn't raise capital very easily, because the stock is only worth $1, but he couldn't be bought out without selling some of his shares.

Example2: Neflix. Suppose the current execs only own 10% of the stocks. 90% is in the hands of the public. Netflix drops to $15. Someone comes in and offers to buy at $20, and buys 90% of the shares. Now they own Netflix and can tell the execs to fuck off, and restructure everything.

Unless a) there is someone to buy the majority of the shares, and b) the company doesn't need to sell more shares to make money, then the price of the stock rise or fall doesn't do anything but affect the people that hold stock as an investment.
